title: Existence of a separable closure; it is Galois over every intermediate field
statement: Let $k$ be a field. (1) There is a field extension $\bar k/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] such that $\bar k$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] and $\bar k/k$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] (a separable algebraic closure of $k$). (2) For any such $\bar k$ and any subfield $k'$ with $k\subseteq k'\subseteq\bar k$: the extension $\bar k/k'$ is separable algebraic and normal (for every $\alpha\in\bar k$ the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k'$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\bar k[T]$), i.e. $\bar k/k'$ is Galois; and $k'/k$ is separable algebraic.

source.place: Fields, Theorem Tag 09GT (theorem-existence-algebraic-closure) and Lemma Tag 09HC (lemma-separable-elements, line 1435: the separable elements of an algebraic closure form a subfield); Definition Tag 030J (definition-separable-algebraic, line 3723, (4)-(5): normal, Galois); Lemma Tag 09I2 (lemma-galois-goes-up) and Lemma Tag 09H2 (lemma-separable-goes-up, line 1187); separable algebraic over a subfield of the bottom: every element of k' is separable over k by definition
